newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air travellers suffer Easter misery in France.
newsitem.headline: Air travellers suffer Easter misery in France.

text.p: Easter weekend air travellers faced major disruption on France's domestic airlines because of a surprise strike on Friday.
A surprise stoppage by ground staff at state-owned Air France Europe, which runs domestic and some European flights, caused long delays at Paris' Orly airport and major cancellations.
A company spokeswoman said all Air France Europe flights were being cancelled on Saturday due to the ground staff strike. All flights were grounded on Friday evening.

"Due to the surprise strike by certain categories of ground staff, the management of Air France Europe are unable to resume normal service. The management has decided to cancel all flights on Saturday," she said.
The workers were protesting against the merging of their pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France when the two companies merge on September 1.
Air France Europe pilots and flight crew have called a two-day strike over pay and conditions for next Monday and Tuesday but the company said all flights would be maintained.
"Traffic will be completely assured with hardly any chartering," a company spokeswoman said.

Pilots and ground staff at British Airways Plc's French subsidiary, TAT European Airlines, meanwhile staged a 24-hour strike, forcing the cancellation of about three-quarters of the airline's 180 scheduled flights on Friday.
A company spokesman said only 40 to 50 flights would go ahead because of the strike against restructuring plans.
